name: viewer
desc: Read your tasks on your phone, from a server you own
author: Amenbo

config.label: Where to carry
config.help: Whether this may carry to your own server on Cloudflare. It can only take the place away: ticking it still needs the server to exist before anything reaches it, and "3. Set up the server on Cloudflare" is what makes one. Ticking nothing is an answer and it is honoured: the plugin stays enabled and carries nowhere.

config.label: Your server's URL on Cloudflare
config.help: "3. Set up the server on Cloudflare" writes this when it makes the server. There is nothing to type.

config.label: API token the server takes writes with
config.help: "3. Set up the server on Cloudflare" generates this. There is nothing to type.

config.label: Key your tasks are encrypted with
config.help: "3. Set up the server on Cloudflare" generates this. There is nothing to type - the phone is given it by the QR, never over the network.

actions.label: 1. Get the app on your phone
3. Set up the server on Cloudflare
5. See whether a phone is paired

agent.when: Setting up the phone viewer, pairing a phone with it, or carrying by hand what has not reached one yet

commands.does: Puts the store page for Amenbo Viewer on a QR the phone's camera reads — one code for iPhone, one for Android — so the address is not carried to the phone by hand. Asks nothing and keeps nothing
Opens Cloudflare's token screen in the browser, with the three permissions setup needs already ticked, and ends there. Asks nothing and keeps nothing — the token the page makes is pasted into setup
Stands up the Worker and its database in the user's own Cloudflare account, and generates the token and key. Takes a Cloudflare API token from the settings screen, a terminal or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
Carries by hand what has not reached the phone yet, encrypting a record at a time, over every route that is configured. The hook does this per write, so this is for what was left behind
Says whether a phone may read, and since when, by asking the store. There is one read code, so the answer is present or absent rather than a list
Undoes the pairing: takes the read code away, so whatever was holding it stops reading. Takes nothing — there is one code, so there is nothing to name
Pairs a phone: issues the read code, registers its hash, puts endpoint/code/key on a QR the camera reads, off the network. Issuing again replaces it; --terminal draws the code here
Compares what the phone's server holds with what this PC holds and carries the difference, without emptying anything. Counts on the first run and sends on the second — or on the first with --send
Says where records are reaching right now — the places ticked under 'Where to carry' that also exist. Reads nothing over the network; the settings screen raises it, and a terminal may too
